speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance. To help me assess your condition, could you please describe exactly how the dizziness feels, such as whether the room spins or if you just feel off-balance?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Vestibular Neuritis.

I have noted your history of increased garlic intake and use of diphenhydramine, but since your dizziness is constant and not clearly triggered by head movements, I do not suspect BPPV. Could you tell me if you have had any fever, sore throat, or ear pain in the last few days?
